rfis: Site control: provide executed lease/option/purchase agreements for parcel 13401900020000 and all adjacent parcels, total controlled acreage (benchmark ~6 ac/MW => ~600 ac for 100 MW), term length, extension rights, and assignment/cure provisions.
Title: provide a current ALTA title commitment with all Schedule B exceptions plus an ALTA/NSPS survey showing easements, access rights, and encumbrances.

Zoning: state the parcel's Sacramento County zoning designation and General Plan land-use designation; provide any county correspondence, pre-application meeting notes, or prior use-permit research for solar+storage on the parcel.
Agricultural status: provide the parcel's Williamson Act contract status (contract number, nonrenewal status) and FMMP Important Farmland classification (Prime/Statewide/Unique/Grazing).

Interconnection: provide the CAISO interconnection request, queue position and cluster number, all completed study reports, deliverability election (FCDS vs Energy-Only), network-upgrade cost estimates, and interconnection financial security postings to date.
Offtake: provide any executed PPA, LOI, or term sheet; identify the counterparty, contracted MW/MWh versus P50, tenor, price, deliverability requirements, and Resource Adequacy obligations.

CAPEX: provide the full capital cost estimate in $/Wac with EPC term sheet, owner-furnished equipment split, and contingency percentage, for testing against the $1.43-1.56/Wac LBNL/NREL benchmark band.

Equipment: provide module supply agreement or shortlisted vendors with pricing; BESS integrator, chemistry, and integrator agreement status; GSU/main power transformer procurement plan with quoted lead times and factory slot reservations.

Tax credits: provide the beginning-of-construction strategy under OBBBA (5% safe harbor vs physical work test), target BOC date relative to the July 4, 2026 deadline, supporting invoices/contracts, ITC vs PTC election analysis, and FEOC/material-assistance compliance plan for all components.

Permitting/CEQA: provide the full permit matrix, CEQA document status (or CEC AB 205 Opt-In filing status), protocol-level biological survey reports (Swainson's hawk, giant garter snake, burrowing owl, vernal pool species), aquatic resources delineation, and cultural resources survey.
BESS safety: provide UL 9540A test reports for the selected BESS product, NFPA 855 compliance design narrative, and records of any fire-authority consultation.
Financials: provide the project financial model with P50/P90 energy yield, degradation, DSCR by case, debt sizing, tax-equity structure, and ITC/PTC monetization plan.

Schedule: provide the integrated milestone schedule from NTP to COD showing permitting, interconnection construction, network upgrades, equipment delivery (especially GSU at 128-144 weeks), and commissioning.
Community: provide the community engagement plan, records of outreach, any known opposition, and the draft decommissioning plan with cost estimate and proposed financial assurance.
Water/drainage: provide construction and operations water source (dust control, panel washing), drainage/stormwater plan, and any well or water-district agreements.

agency_actions.agency: Sacramento County Planning and Environmental Review (PER)
agency_actions.action: Request a formal zoning verification letter for parcel 13401900020000 and a pre-application meeting to confirm whether utility-scale solar+storage is a permitted or conditionally permitted use (CUP under the Sacramento County Zoning Code), and to scope the CEQA pathway with the County as lead agency.
agency_actions.why: Zoning is an unresolved kill criterion: if the parcel is ag-zoned and solar is prohibited or requires discretionary approval with farmland conflicts, the local route may be blocked; this determines whether the CEC Opt-In fallback is needed.

agency_actions.agency: California Department of Conservation, Division of Land Resource Protection (with Sacramento County Agricultural Commissioner)
agency_actions.action: Obtain the parcel's FMMP Important Farmland classification and confirm Williamson Act contract status, nonrenewal/cancellation feasibility, and cancellation-cost exposure.
agency_actions.why: Prime/Statewide farmland or an active Williamson Act contract can block or materially delay permitting and triggers CEQA farmland-conversion analysis and potential mitigation.

agency_actions.agency: California Energy Commission (CEC) - Opt-In Certification Program (AB 205, Public Resources Code sec. 25545)
agency_actions.action: Request an eligibility consultation for Opt-In Certification (eligible if >=50 MW PV plus >=200 MWh BESS) as the state-level permitting fallback that preempts local zoning and substitutes for CEQA review.
agency_actions.why: If Sacramento County zoning is prohibitive or the CUP timeline is unworkable, the CEC Opt-In route is the only viable path to permit a 100 MW solar+storage facility on this parcel.
agency_actions.deadline: Within 60 days; file notice of intent before local-path go/no-go decision

agency_actions.agency: California ISO (CAISO) - Generator Interconnection and Deliverability Allocation Procedures
agency_actions.action: Verify the project's queue position and cluster status under the reformed cluster process (Cluster 15), obtain study results and network-upgrade cost estimates, and confirm the deliverability (FCDS) allocation timeline and financial security posting schedule.
agency_actions.why: No queue position is evidenced; CAISO's reformed process carries ~5-year IR-to-COD norms, ~20% historical success rates, and unquantified network-upgrade cost shock risk that directly drives CAPEX and schedule.
agency_actions.deadline: Within 30 days; align with next CAISO cluster application window if not yet queued

agency_actions.agency: South Sacramento Habitat Conservation Plan (SSHCP) - Sacramento County / SSHCP Joint Powers Authority
agency_actions.action: Confirm parcel coverage under the SSHCP, determine covered-species take authorization pathway (giant garter snake, Swainson's hawk), applicable fees, and required avoidance/minimization measures.
agency_actions.why: The parcel sits in SSHCP territory; coverage determines whether ESA/CESA take authorization is streamlined or requires separate USFWS/CDFW consultation, a major schedule driver.

agency_actions.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW), North Central Region
agency_actions.action: Scope need for a Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement (Fish and Game Code sec. 1602) and state-listed species consultation if impacts fall outside SSHCP coverage.
agency_actions.why: Any jurisdictional stream/wetland crossings or listed-species take outside the SSHCP requires CDFW authorization before construction.
agency_actions.deadline: Within 90 days, following aquatic resources delineation

agency_actions.agency: Central Valley Regional Water Quality Control Board (Region 5S)
agency_actions.action: Enroll under the Construction General Permit (SWPPP) and, if a federal CWA sec. 404 permit is required, obtain sec. 401 water quality certification.
agency_actions.why: Construction stormwater coverage is mandatory before ground disturbance; 401 certification is a federal-permit dependency if wetlands/waters are impacted.
agency_actions.deadline: SWPPP before any ground disturbance; 401 determination within 90 days of delineation

agency_actions.agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Sacramento District
agency_actions.action: Submit an approved jurisdictional determination request and, if waters of the U.S. are impacted, secure CWA sec. 404 authorization (nationwide permit or individual permit).
agency_actions.why: Vernal pools and seasonal wetlands common in south Sacramento County may be federally jurisdictional; 404 permitting is a long-lead item that gates construction.
agency_actions.deadline: AJD request within 90 days of delineation

agency_actions.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Sacramento Fish and Wildlife Office
agency_actions.action: Confirm whether ESA sec. 7 consultation is needed (via USACE nexus) or whether SSHCP incidental take coverage applies for giant garter snake and vernal pool species.
agency_actions.why: Federal take authorization outside the SSHCP can add 12+ months; early confirmation de-risks the schedule.

agency_actions.agency: Sacramento Metropolitan Fire District (or applicable fire authority having jurisdiction)
agency_actions.action: Obtain BESS fire-protection plan review under NFPA 855 and the California Fire Code, including UL 9540A-based hazard mitigation analysis and emergency response plan approval.
agency_actions.why: BESS fire-safety approval is a building-permit precondition and a lender/insurer requirement; no safety stack is currently evidenced.

agency_actions.agency: Sacramento Municipal Utility District (SMUD) and/or Pacific Gas & Electric (as applicable to the point of interconnection)
agency_actions.action: Confirm the transmission/distribution owner at the point of interconnection, obtain facility study scope, and verify any distribution-level or wholesale distribution interconnection requirements.
agency_actions.why: Parcel 13401900020000 is in Sacramento County where SMUD is the balancing-adjacent utility; the interconnection facilities and network upgrades depend on the interconnecting utility's standards and construction timeline.

agency_actions.action: Monitor and position for CPUC-jurisdictional procurement windows (e.g., the 6 GW NQC central procurement and LSE RFOs) and confirm Resource Adequacy counting rules applicable to the hybrid configuration.
agency_actions.why: Macro procurement tailwinds exist but nothing project-specific; aligning COD and deliverability with CPUC procurement cycles is the path to bankable offtake.
agency_actions.deadline: Ongoing; map to next solicitation cycle within 60 days

agency_actions.agency: Sacramento County Department of Airports / FAA (if within airport influence area)
agency_actions.action: Screen the parcel for airport land-use compatibility (ALUC) and file FAA Form 7460-1 notices if glare or structure heights trigger review.
agency_actions.why: PV glare near Mather, Executive, or McClellan airspace can require mitigation or redesign; unscreened, it is a late-stage permitting surprise.

verification_requests: Offtake: independently verify with the named counterparty (once identified) the existence and status of any PPA/LOI/term sheet, including authorized signatory, board approvals, and credit support terms; if none exists, obtain written confirmation from the developer that no offtake discussions are active.

Interconnection: verify directly with CAISO (via the developer's interconnection customer contact and queue data) the queue position, cluster study results, deliverability status, and network-upgrade cost allocation; do not rely on developer summaries.

GSU/transformer lead times: obtain written quotations from at least two transformer manufacturers (e.g., Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy, GE Vernova, Hyundai) confirming current lead times (benchmark 128-144 weeks), slot availability, and price validity.

Module supply: verify with shortlisted module suppliers the quoted pricing, delivery windows, domestic-content eligibility, and FEOC/material-assistance compliance documentation for OBBBA credit eligibility.
BESS integrator: verify UL 9540A test reports directly with the integrator and the testing laboratory, and confirm production capacity and delivery slots for the target COD.
Title: order an independent title search/commitment from a national title insurer rather than relying on developer-provided documents.
Williamson Act/FMMP: verify contract status directly with Sacramento County and the Department of Conservation rather than developer representations.

Benchmark validation: commission an independent engineer to validate CAPEX against the $1.43-1.56/Wac band, energy yield (P50/P90), and the >=80% P50 contracted bankability norm once data is delivered.
Tax counsel: obtain an independent tax opinion on BOC strategy sufficiency under OBBBA and FEOC compliance before relying on any ITC/PTC value in the model.
Community: conduct independent outreach to Sacramento County supervisor's office and local community groups to verify the developer's community-engagement claims and identify opposition risk.
conditions_precedent: CP-1 (Kill criterion - zoning): Written confirmation of a viable permitting path - either Sacramento County zoning verification that solar+storage is permitted/conditionally permitted with a credible CUP timeline, or a filed CEC AB 205 Opt-In Certification notice of intent with CEC eligibility confirmation.

CP-2 (Kill criterion - tax credits): A complete beginning-of-construction evidence package demonstrating BOC on or before July 4, 2026 (5% safe harbor invoices/binding contracts or physical-work documentation), supported by an independent tax opinion, plus a FEOC/material-assistance compliance plan.

CP-3 (Site control): Executed site-control documents covering >=600 acres (or an independently verified sufficiency analysis at the project's actual design density), with term through at least 30 years or COD plus extensions, and a clean ALTA title commitment with no fatal encumbrances.

CP-4 (Interconnection): Evidence of an active CAISO queue position with completed or in-progress cluster studies, quantified network-upgrade cost exposure, a deliverability (FCDS) plan, and a financial-security posting schedule consistent with the project schedule.

CP-5 (Offtake): An executed PPA or binding term sheet with a creditworthy counterparty covering >=80% of P50 energy, or a credible, dated procurement strategy mapped to specific CPUC/LSE solicitation windows.

CP-6 (CAPEX/financials): A full financial model with CAPEX within or justified against the $1.43-1.56/Wac benchmark band, DSCR by case, contingency >=5%, and a tax-credit monetization plan (transferability or tax equity).

CP-7 (Equipment): Executed or near-final supply agreements for modules and BESS with delivery schedules consistent with COD, and a GSU procurement plan with reserved factory slots addressing the 128-144 week lead time.
CP-8 (BESS safety): UL 9540A reports for the selected product, an NFPA 855-compliant design, and written fire-authority concurrence.

CP-9 (Environmental): Completed protocol-level biological surveys, aquatic resources delineation, SSHCP coverage determination, and a CEQA/CEC permitting schedule with no unresolved fatal-flaw findings.
CP-10 (Schedule): An integrated schedule demonstrating that permitting, interconnection construction, network upgrades, and long-lead equipment delivery support the stated COD, with float identified.

CP-11 (Decommissioning/community): A draft decommissioning plan with cost estimate and proposed financial assurance mechanism, plus documented community engagement with no unmitigated organized opposition.
